why: PRINCIPLES 7, for controlroom. The claim every plugin host makes is that its `schema.json` plus its README is enough for an agent to write a working plugin in one turn, and that `controlroom check` tells it so without a human reading the output. This is controlroom's half, from the day its plugin surface (R10) exists.
prompt: Read packages/controlroom/src/schema.json and packages/controlroom/README.md. Write a controlroom plugin to the file evals/results/vim-keys-plugin.mjs. It must be a single ES module with a default export, must be named "vim-keys", and must contribute one keymap called "vim" that binds h to tab.prev and l to tab.next, with both actions labelled "switch tab". Then verify it by running: node packages/controlroom/dist/cli.js check evals/results/vim-keys-plugin.mjs — and if that command exits non-zero, fix the plugin until it exits zero. Do not modify anything under packages/.

expect.value: node packages/controlroom/dist/cli.js check evals/results/vim-keys-plugin.mjs | grep -q '^vim-keys: ok'
node packages/controlroom/dist/cli.js check evals/results/vim-keys-plugin.mjs | grep -q 'hint: h/l switch tab'
